Chess against the Sphinx

You play White: drag a piece to its square, or click it and then the square. The Sphinx answers each move, but only with a move this app lists as legal: anything else is refused and the rules play for it. The chat never reaches its moves.

How it ends. You win by checkmating the Sphinx. You lose if it checkmates you, or if you resign. Stalemate, the same position three times, fifty moves with no capture or pawn move, and too little material left to mate are draws.

Tidewheel

A sea nobody hosts, that everyone can check.

Press the sea to plant a whirl.
joiningtick -era of -, turns in -chain -

Nobody sends you the sea.

It is 9,216 cells obeying one rule, and your browser is computing it now. The server only keeps the order of things: once a second it sends what was done that tick, which is the touches people planted and a hash chained onto the ticks before it. Anyone with the same law and the same touches gets the same sea.

The server cannot see the sea, so the pages vouch for it. Every 60 ticks each one hashes its sea and tells the server; the first also sends the sea itself, which becomes a fossil, and the rest are counted as agreeing or not. The count is evidence: anonymous pages can lie.

Replay a fossil and your browser takes the one before it and the touches in between, runs the law 60 times and compares its hash with the one kept. Fork starts a sea of your own from it.

The law is /law.js. This page runs the law whose sha256 is ... and the server says the world's is ....
